items.q: How would you design a metadata-driven pipeline that loads 100 tables without creating 100 pipelines?
items.a:
Use one generic pipeline driven by a control table instead of 100 pipelines.
• Control table: source schema/table, target path, load type (full/incremental), watermark column, active flag.
• Lookup reads the active rows → ForEach (parallel, batch count tuned to what the source can handle) → Copy activity with parameterised source and sink datasets (@item().table_name).
• A stored procedure updates the watermark and writes an audit row per table.
Adding a table is just a new row — no pipeline change or redeploy.

items.q: What is the difference between a linked service and a dataset?
items.a: A linked service is the connection (where): server, database, authentication, usually via Key Vault or managed identity. A dataset is the data (what): a specific table, file or folder, its format and schema, reached through a linked service. One linked service can serve many datasets.

items.q: How would you implement an incremental load using a watermark column?
items.a:
Store the last successful watermark (max modified_date) in a control table.
1. Lookup the old watermark and the new maximum from the source.
2. Copy only rows with modified_date > old AND <= new.
3. MERGE into the target on the business key.
4. Update the watermark only after the copy succeeds, so a failed run is simply retried.
Use a small overlap window plus MERGE to catch late commits without duplicates.

items.q: A daily file does not arrive on time. How would you alert instead of failing the pipeline?
items.a:
Don't let a missing file fail the pipeline.
• Validation activity (timeout + sleep interval), or Get Metadata with the 'exists' field inside an Until loop, to wait for the file.
• If Condition: when the file exists → run the copy; when it doesn't → call a Logic App/webhook that emails or posts to Teams 'file not received for <date>', log a MISSING status and end cleanly.
• Optionally switch to a storage event trigger so the pipeline starts when the file actually lands.
